    Description
    BaseLevelConfig
    Describes what is being tuned and on what training set — the part of a TrainingRequest that is independent of how the meta-optimizer searches the parameter space (see MetaSearchConfig) and of where a particular run writes its results (see TrainingRequest.outputDirectory()) — everything here is meant to be reused, unchanged, across many training requests, loaded by name via BaseLevelConfigurationReader.
    BaseLevelConfigurationReader
    Loads a BaseLevelConfig from a base-level configuration file by name (e.g.
    BaseLevelConfigurationWriter
    Writes a BaseLevelConfig out to a base-level configuration file readable by BaseLevelConfigurationReader — the counterpart that lets cli.training.generators build a BaseLevelConfig in Java (compiler-checked field types and list sizes) and turn it into the same kind of reusable, named file a hand-written one would be, instead of keeping the values duplicated between Java source and a YAML fixture.
    DescribeMain
    Prints a single, machine-readable YAML manifest to stdout describing everything cli.training can resolve today: registered base algorithms, meta-optimizer algorithms, training problems, indicators, the names available under each reusable resource directory, and the shape of request.yaml/baseLevel/metaSearch themselves.
    FlatMetaSearchConfig

    MetaSearchConfig
    How the meta-optimizer searches the base-level algorithm's parameter space — the part of a TrainingRequest that depends on the meta-level encoding, loaded from a named, reusable meta-optimizer configuration file via MetaOptimizerConfigurationReader (e.g.
    ProblemSpec
    Identifies a training problem: a class (a short, curated name registered in ProblemRegistry, or a fully-qualified class name resolved by reflection) plus the constructor arguments it needs, if any.
    TrainingRequest
    Prototype request describing a single meta-optimization training run: BaseLevelConfig (what is being tuned, and on what training set — independent of the meta-level encoding), MetaSearchConfig (how the meta-optimizer searches that parameter space, which differs entirely between the flat and tree encodings — see FlatMetaSearchConfig and TreeMetaSearchConfig), and three fields specific to monitoring *this* run rather than to the algorithm itself: outputDirectory (where results are written), writeFrequency (how often, in evaluations, CONFIGURATIONS.csv/INDICATORS.csv are written — defaults to 100, roughly one generation, not every single evaluation) and statusFrequency (how often status.yaml/the log are updated — also defaults to 100).
    TrainingRunner
    Runs a single <meta-optimizer>-tunes-<base-level-algorithm> meta-optimization training job described by a TrainingRequest, reusing the same builder/observer/output pipeline as the org.uma.evolver.example.training reference examples — one pipeline per meta-level encoding (see FlatMetaSearchConfig, TreeMetaSearchConfig).
    TrainingRunnerMain
    Minimal CLI entry point for TrainingRunner: a single argument (path to a TrainingRequest YAML file) replaces the ad hoc, hardcoded main(String[] args) pattern used by the other org.uma.evolver.example.training classes.
    TreeMetaSearchConfig
    Meta-search configuration for the derivation tree encoding, resolved via MetaAlgorithmRegistry.
